stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, Public Law 88-452; quotations are from the act.
stimulus.text:
Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act, signed August 20, 1964. The act said it was the policy of the United States "to eliminate the paradox of poverty in the midst of plenty" by opening to everyone "the opportunity for education and training, the opportunity to work, and the opportunity to live in decency and dignity."

It created the Office of Economic Opportunity to run new programs: the Job Corps, which gave young people ages 16 to 21 education and job training at residential centers; Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA), which sent volunteers to help poor communities; and community action programs, run "with the maximum feasible participation" of residents.

stem: VISTA, as described in the passage, was most similar to which earlier program?

options.text: The Tennessee Valley Authority, which built dams
options.misconception: VISTA sent volunteers to help poor communities; it did not build dams.

options.text: The Peace Corps, which sent volunteers abroad
The Civilian Conservation Corps, which paid soldiers
options.misconception: Background: the Civilian Conservation Corps employed young men on conservation work, and it did not pay soldiers.

options.text: The Social Security system, which paid retirees
options.misconception: VISTA sent volunteers to poor communities; it did not pay retirees.

rationales.A: VISTA sent volunteers to help poor communities; it did not build dams.
rationales.B: Background: the Peace Corps sent volunteers abroad, while VISTA sent volunteers to help poor communities at home.
rationales.C: Background: the Civilian Conservation Corps employed young men on conservation work in the 1930s, which is not volunteer service to poor communities.
rationales.D: VISTA sent volunteers to poor communities; it did not pay retirees.
rationales.general:
1. VISTA sent volunteers to help poor communities.
2. The key word is volunteers: people giving time rather than taking pay.
3. Background: the Peace Corps did the same work abroad, sending volunteers to other countries.
4. VISTA was therefore the same volunteer idea turned toward home.
Remember: Match programs by what people do in them, not by their names.
